sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: I'm sorry to do this, but I'm going to take you back to January 6th, 2021.
sentences.zh: 抱歉要这么做，但我得带大家回到2021年1月6日。

sentences.en: I can see at least half a dozen protesters scaling, literally climbing.
sentences.zh: 我至少能看到六名抗议者在攀爬，真的是在往上爬。

sentences.en: A violent mob of Trump supporters attempted to overturn the 2020 election results with physical force.
sentences.zh: 一群暴力的特朗普支持者试图通过武力推翻2020年的选举结果。

sentences.en: They broke into the Capitol, disrupted the Electoral College vote, and occupied the building for hours.
sentences.zh: 他们闯入国会大厦，扰乱了选举人团投票，并占领了该建筑数小时。

sentences.en: Like most of you, I had my butt clenched that day, watching the insurrection unfold on television.
sentences.zh: 和你们大多数人一样，那天我紧张得不得了，在电视上看着这场暴乱发生。

sentences.en: Producer Vivian Leigh.
sentences.zh: 制片人薇薇安·李。

sentences.en: I also happened to be watching that news coverage with my mom.
sentences.zh: 当时我恰好和我妈一起看着新闻报道。

sentences.en: I see every channel.
sentences.zh: 我什么频道都看。

sentences.en: I watch ABC, I watch CBS, I watch CNN, I watch Fox.
sentences.zh: 我看ABC，看CBS，看CNN，也看福克斯。

sentences.en: Every, every perspective.
sentences.zh: 每一个，每一个视角都看。

sentences.en: This is my mom, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，这是我妈。

sentences.en: Do you want to say hi to my boss real fast?
sentences.zh: 你想快点跟我老板打个招呼吗？

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Roman.
sentences.zh: 罗曼。

sentences.en: Hi, Roman.
sentences.zh: 你好，罗曼。

sentences.en: This is Vivian's mom.
sentences.zh: 这是薇薇安的妈妈。

sentences.en: Hey, mom.
sentences.zh: 嘿，妈。

sentences.en: So that day during the insurrection, yes, we were both horrified.
sentences.zh: 所以那天暴乱期间，是的，我们俩都感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: And yes, we were both worried about the state of democracy.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们俩也都为民主的现状感到担忧。

sentences.en: But as my mom and I scanned the aerial shots of the rioters marching down Pennsylvania Avenue,
sentences.zh: 但当我和我妈扫视着暴徒们沿宾夕法尼亚大道游行的航拍镜头时，

sentences.en: we also couldn't help but notice the dizzying amount of different types of flags there that day.
sentences.zh: 我们也不禁注意到那天现场旗帜的种类多得令人眼花缭乱。

sentences.en: Aside from seeing the obvious choices like the U.S.
sentences.zh: 除了看到像美国国旗

sentences.en: or MAGA flag, there were some that were just really hideous graphic designs,
sentences.zh: 或“让美国再次伟大”（MAGA）旗帜这种显而易见的选择外，还有一些设计极其丑陋的旗帜，

sentences.en: like the flag of Trump photoshopped as Rambo or Kelvin from Kelvin and Hobbes peeing on Biden.
sentences.zh: 比如把特朗普PS成兰博的旗帜，或者《卡尔文与霍布斯》里的卡尔文对着拜登撒尿的旗帜。

sentences.en: Stupid.
sentences.zh: 真蠢。

sentences.en: But just seemingly, you know, not attract me.
sentences.zh: 但看起来，你知道，并不吸引我。

sentences.en: They don't attract me either, mom.
sentences.zh: 它们也不吸引我，妈。

sentences.en: Then there were the flags that, even for a person like me, who spends a lot of time thinking about flags, couldn't decode.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一些旗帜，即使是对我这种花大量时间研究旗帜的人来说，也无法解读。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't understand what to stand for some flag, you know.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我不知道有些旗帜代表什么，你知道的。

sentences.en: What is it?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: Some for brown boys, some for white supremacists.
sentences.zh: 有些是给棕色人种男孩的，有些是给白人至上主义者的。

sentences.en: Yeah, supremacists.
sentences.zh: 是的，至上主义者。

sentences.en: But I don't know what to stand for because I'm not on here.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道它们代表什么，因为我不是那一伙的。

sentences.en: But flying from the balcony of the Capitol building along some of these inscrutable symbols was a flag that my mom instantly recognized.
sentences.zh: 但在国会大厦阳台上，在这些令人费解的符号旁边飘扬的，是一面我妈一眼就认出来的旗帜。

sentences.en: Actually, she more than just recognized it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她不仅仅是认出了它。

sentences.en: Ha, that one.
sentences.zh: 哈，那面旗。

sentences.en: That's the one that we love, we cherish all my life.
sentences.zh: 那是我一生中热爱、珍视的旗帜。

sentences.en: It was such a simple design that most people probably didn't even notice it.
sentences.zh: 它的设计非常简单，大多数人可能根本没注意到它。

sentences.en: Bright yellow with three red horizontal stripes across the center.
sentences.zh: 亮黄色底，中间有三条红色横杠。

sentences.en: This was the flag of South Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 这就是南越国旗。

sentences.en: This is the flag that she grew up with.
sentences.zh: 这是她从小就熟悉的旗帜。

sentences.en: It reminds her of some of the best years of her life.
sentences.zh: 它让她想起自己一生中最美好的岁月。

sentences.en: So, when she saw it flying alongside banners that overtly signaled hate, racism, and misogyny that day, it felt like it was telling the rest of the world that, hey,
sentences.zh: 所以，当那天她看到它与那些公然散发仇恨、种族主义和厌女情绪的横幅一起飘扬时，感觉就像是在告诉全世界，嘿，

sentences.en: this flag stands for all those things, too.
sentences.zh: 这面旗帜也代表了所有那些东西。

sentences.en: I feel ashamed because the people raised it at the wrong day, the wrong event.
sentences.zh: 我感到羞愧，因为人们在错误的日子、错误的场合举起了它。

sentences.en: The flag of South Vietnam and what it should stand for is a really contentious issue for the Vietnamese-American community.
sentences.zh: 南越国旗及其应代表的含义，对于越南裔美国人社区来说是一个极具争议的问题。

sentences.en: And while seeing it raised at the insurrection felt like the wrong way to use this flag for my mom, the right way to use it was hard for her to put into words.
sentences.zh: 虽然看到它在暴乱中被举起，让我妈觉得这是对这面旗帜的错误使用，但正确的用法她却很难用言语表达。

sentences.en: How is it supposed to be used?
sentences.zh: 它到底应该怎么用呢？

sentences.en: I don't know how to say it, let me see.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该怎么说，让我想想。

sentences.en: Yeah, take your time.
sentences.zh: 好的，不着急。

sentences.en: Just stop it, stop it.
sentences.zh: 别说了，停下。

sentences.en: No, it's okay.
sentences.zh: 不，没关系。

sentences.en: Just take your time.
sentences.zh: 慢慢来就好。

sentences.en: I'm not going to—
sentences.zh: 我不是要——

sentences.en: Let me think about this one a little bit, because it's a little bit serious, you know?
sentences.zh: 让我仔细想想这个问题，因为它有点严肃，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So, I have to think in something that I should say.
sentences.zh: 所以，我得好好斟酌一下该说什么。

sentences.en: If I were to ask you to draw the Vietnamese flag, and that's all I specified, which one would you draw?
sentences.zh: 如果我让你画出越南国旗，而且我只提了这一点，你会画哪一面？

sentences.en: That's a good one.
sentences.zh: 这问题问得好。

sentences.en: I don't know if I can do that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我能不能做到。

sentences.en: I mean, like, I guess, you know, like any academic, right, I would say, like, give me more information.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就像任何学者一样，对吧，我会说，给我更多信息。

sentences.en: Ha ha ha ha!
sentences.zh: 哈哈哈哈！

sentences.en: This is Tuan Huang.
sentences.zh: 这位是黄团（Tuan Huang）。

sentences.en: He's a historian and associate professor at Pepperdine University, who did not fall for my gotcha journalism.
sentences.zh: 他是一位历史学家，也是佩珀代因大学的副教授，他没有掉进我设下的“陷阱式”采访圈套。

sentences.en: A lot like myself, he didn't think to explore the history of the flag until fairly recently.
sentences.zh: 和我一样，他直到最近才想到去探究这面旗帜的历史。

sentences.en: I mean, I did not plan at all to look into the history of the foreigners' flag.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我完全没打算去研究外国旗帜的历史。

sentences.en: And then, like, January 6th happened, and then boom!
sentences.zh: 然后，1月6日事件发生了，接着，砰！

sentences.en: It's just like, oh, my God, I need to look into this.
sentences.zh: 当时的感觉就是，天哪，我必须研究一下这个。

sentences.en: There were actually several confounding international flags present at the Capitol riot that day.
sentences.zh: 那天在国会大厦骚乱现场，确实出现了几面令人困惑的国际旗帜。

sentences.en: The Canadian, Indian, and South Korean flags were all spotted somewhere in the mayhem.
sentences.zh: 在混乱中，有人在某处看到了加拿大、印度和韩国的国旗。

sentences.en: But what was peculiar about the Vietnamese flag being there is that it's not technically the flag of Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 但越南国旗出现在那里之所以奇怪，是因为从技术上讲，它并不是越南现在的国旗。

sentences.en: It's the flag of the Republic of Vietnam, a country that no longer exists.
sentences.zh: 它是越南共和国的国旗，而那个国家已经不复存在了。

sentences.en: The Republic of Vietnam, or more commonly known as South Vietnam, was in a way a reaction to a reaction to colonialism.
sentences.zh: 越南共和国，也就是大家更熟知的南越，在某种程度上是对殖民主义的一种反抗。

sentences.en: Because the country has spent over a thousand years being ruled by outside forces.
sentences.zh: 因为这个国家在过去一千多年里一直被外部势力统治。

sentences.en: Colonialism, you know, was massively important in the history of Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 你知道，殖民主义在越南历史上有着极其重要的影响。

sentences.en: Vietnam spent much of its early history ruled by China.
sentences.zh: 越南早期历史的大部分时间都处于中国的统治之下。

sentences.en: And then in the mid-1800s, Vietnam came under the control of outside powers again.
sentences.zh: 到了19世纪中期，越南再次受到外部势力的控制。

sentences.en: This time, France.
sentences.zh: 这次是法国。

sentences.en: We spent a lot of time dragging British colonialism on the show, but today we're coming for the French.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目里花了很多时间抨击英国殖民主义，但今天我们要针对法国。

sentences.en: For decades, France exploited Vietnam's natural resources, made the poor more poor, and suppressed Vietnamese identity.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，法国掠夺了越南的自然资源，让穷人更穷，并压制了越南人的民族认同。

sentences.en: Even banning the word Vietnam from the region because it was associated with self-determination.
sentences.zh: 甚至在当地禁用了“越南”这个词，因为它与民族自决联系在一起。

sentences.en: The Vietnamese, right, they hated it.
sentences.zh: 越南人，对吧，他们恨透了这一点。

sentences.en: They did not want to be ruled by the French in this case.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，他们不想被法国人统治。

sentences.en: Another big consequence of colonialism was that it led different Vietnamese people into two clashing political ideologies.
sentences.zh: 殖民主义的另一个重大后果是，它导致越南人分成了两种相互冲突的政治意识形态。

sentences.en: Some groups were leaning towards reform, right?
sentences.zh: 一些群体倾向于改革，对吧？

sentences.en: Some groups were leaning towards more radical ideology like communism.
sentences.zh: 一些群体倾向于更激进的意识形态，比如共产主义。

sentences.en: There were those who believed that, yes, colonialism is bad, but also wanted to stay closely aligned with the United States.
sentences.zh: 还有一些人认为，是的，殖民主义是不好的，但他们也希望与美国保持密切一致。

sentences.en: But leaders like Ho Chi Minh in the North believed that there would be no flourishing under any form of imperialism.
sentences.zh: 但像北方的胡志明这样的领导人认为，在任何形式的帝国主义统治下都不会有繁荣。

sentences.en: Vietnam needed to be a completely independent and communist state.
sentences.zh: 越南需要成为一个完全独立且共产主义的国家。

sentences.en: Ho Chi Minh and his army, the Viet Minh, defeated the French in 1954, which rattled the Western world.
sentences.zh: 胡志明和他的军队——越盟，在1954年击败了法国人，这震惊了西方世界。

sentences.en: Countries like the U.S.
sentences.zh: 像美国这样的国家

sentences.en: were concerned that communism would continue spreading throughout Southeast Asia.
sentences.zh: 担心共产主义会继续在东南亚蔓延。

sentences.en: The Palais des Nations, where the League of Nations wrestled with international problems many years ago now,
sentences.zh: 万国宫，也就是多年前国际联盟曾在此处理国际问题的地方，

sentences.en: is the handsome setting for the Geneva Conference.
sentences.zh: 是日内瓦会议的举办地。

sentences.en: Korea and Indochina are the chief problems to be solved.
sentences.zh: 朝鲜和印度支那问题是当时亟待解决的主要问题。

sentences.en: During the 1954 Geneva Conference, it was decided that France would withdraw from northern Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 在1954年的日内瓦会议期间，决定法国将从越南北部撤军。

sentences.en: It was also decided that until free elections could be held, the country would be split in two.
sentences.zh: 会议还决定，在举行自由选举之前，国家将被一分为二。

sentences.en: Vietnam was partitioned at the 17th parallel, with a communist country in the north and in the south,
sentences.zh: 越南以北纬17度线为界被分割，北方是一个共产主义国家，而南方，

sentences.en: a country that was nominally democratic with a heavy U.S.
sentences.zh: 是一个名义上民主但深受美国影响的国家。

sentences.en: influence.
sentences.zh: 影响力。

sentences.en: Two separate ideologies, territories, and flags.
sentences.zh: 两个独立的意识形态、领土和旗帜。

sentences.en: The flag of South Vietnam was a yellow field with three thin red stripes running horizontally across the center.
sentences.zh: 南越的旗帜是一块黄色底面，中间有三条横向的红色细条纹。

sentences.en: The yellow symbolized the, uh, people.
sentences.zh: 黄色象征着，呃，人民。

sentences.en: And the three red stripes represented the three distinct regions of the country.
sentences.zh: 而那三条红色条纹代表了该国三个不同的地区。

sentences.en: North, central, and South Vietnam unified under one banner.
sentences.zh: 北越、中越和南越统一在同一面旗帜下。

sentences.en: In the north, leadership wanted the same thing, a unified Vietnam under these same two colors.
sentences.zh: 在北方，领导层也想要同样的东西，即在这两种颜色下统一越南。

sentences.en: But theirs was a different flag, a red field with a bright yellow star at the center.
sentences.zh: 但他们用的是另一面旗帜，红底，中间有一颗明亮的黄星。

sentences.en: The five points of the star were to represent peasants, workers, intellectuals, traders, and soldiers who unite to build socialism.
sentences.zh: 五角星的五个角分别代表农民、工人、知识分子、商人和士兵，他们团结起来建设社会主义。

sentences.en: These two Vietnams clashed in a civil war that lasted for two decades.
sentences.zh: 这两个越南在持续了二十年的内战中发生了冲突。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: wanted South Vietnam to be its anti-communist stronghold in Southeast Asia.
sentences.zh: 希望南越成为其在东南亚的反共堡垒。

sentences.en: But as the war dragged on, it became clearer and clearer that a democratic Vietnam was not possible.
sentences.zh: 但随着战争的拖延，越来越清楚的是，建立一个民主的越南是不可能的。

sentences.en: And so, long story short, right, by 1973, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，长话短说，对吧，到1973年，美国

sentences.en: troops had withdrawn pretty much completely.
sentences.zh: 军队已经基本完全撤离了。

sentences.en: They just, you know, don't want to deal with that war anymore.
sentences.zh: 他们只是，你知道，不想再处理那场战争了。

sentences.en: Here's my mom again.
sentences.zh: 这是我妈妈。

sentences.en: She actually lived in Saigon and was in law school during this time.
sentences.zh: 当时她确实住在西贡，还在读法学院。

sentences.en: They decided, you know, like, to withdraw from the country.
sentences.zh: 他们决定，你知道，撤出这个国家。

sentences.en: And then, you know, we know that we will, you know, lose the fight with communists.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，我们知道我们，你知道，会输掉与共产党的这场战斗。

sentences.en: If South Vietnam fell, anyone associated with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果南越沦陷，任何与美国

sentences.en: government or South Vietnamese military could be a target for the North Vietnamese regime.
sentences.zh: 政府或南越军队有关的人都可能成为北越政权的目标。

sentences.en: My mom had family in the military and also a sister who worked for the Americans, so it wouldn't be safe to stay.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈有亲戚在军队里，还有一个姐姐为美国人工作，所以留下来并不安全。

sentences.en: But because of these connections, she was able to flee right before the city was captured.
sentences.zh: 但正因为这些关系，她在城市被占领前夕得以逃离。

sentences.en: We just packed up some little thing, you know, personal thing, and go.
sentences.zh: 我们只是收拾了一些小东西，你知道，私人物品，然后就走了。

sentences.en: And I remember I only carry all small stuff like personal, like a love letter and memory book from high school and few clothes.
sentences.zh: 我记得我只带了一些小东西，比如私人的东西，像情书、高中的纪念册和几件衣服。

sentences.en: And that's it.
sentences.zh: 就这样。

sentences.en: Just the backpack, you know, nothing else.
sentences.zh: 只有一个背包，你知道，没有别的了。

sentences.en: My mom was a lot more privileged and a hell of a lot luckier than most people in South Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈比南越的大多数人优越得多，也幸运得多。

sentences.en: And she still lost everything.
sentences.zh: 但她还是失去了一切。

sentences.en: Oh, I'm crying when the flight lift off.
sentences.zh: 哦，飞机起飞时我哭了。

sentences.en: And I see the land, you know, down there.
sentences.zh: 我看着下面的土地，你知道。

sentences.en: And my tears just come out a lot.
sentences.zh: 我的眼泪止不住地流。

sentences.en: I know that, you know, I never see it again.
sentences.zh: 我知道，你知道，我再也见不到它了。

sentences.en: She was actually on one of the last planes to leave the country.
sentences.zh: 她实际上是最后一批离开这个国家的飞机之一上的乘客。

sentences.en: The next day, the airport was bombed.
sentences.zh: 第二天，机场就被炸了。

sentences.en: A few days later, North Vietnamese tanks crashed through the gates of the presidential palace in Saigon
sentences.zh: 几天后，北越坦克冲进了西贡总统府的大门，

sentences.en: and took down the flag of South Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 并降下了南越的旗帜。

sentences.en: The war was over.
sentences.zh: 战争结束了。

sentences.en: The conquering tanks burst straight into the presidential palace.
sentences.zh: 征服的坦克直接冲进了总统府。

sentences.en: For the fourth time in a month, the presidential palace had new occupants.
sentences.zh: 一个月内，总统府第四次迎来了新主人。

sentences.en: But these had come to stay.
sentences.zh: 但这些人是来长住的。

sentences.en: April 30th, 1975.
That's the day when South Vietnam fell to the North Vietnamese.
sentences.zh: 那是南越沦陷于北越的日子。

sentences.en: This is Thuy Vo Deng, curator of UC Irvine's Southeast Asian Archive.
sentences.zh: 这位是加州大学欧文分校东南亚档案馆的馆长Thuy Vo Deng。

sentences.en: In Vietnam, it's known as Liberation Day.
sentences.zh: 在越南，这一天被称为解放日。

sentences.en: And in the diaspora, it's often referred to as Ngai Mek Nhu, or the day we lost our homeland, right?
sentences.zh: 而在海外侨民中，它通常被称为“国耻日”，或者我们失去家园的日子，对吧？

sentences.en: Or Ngai Gua Kung, or the day of national resentment.
sentences.zh: 或者“民族怨恨日”。

sentences.en: After the fall of Saigon, the North and South once again became one nation.
sentences.zh: 西贡沦陷后，南北再次成为一个国家。

sentences.en: The new government of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam immediately went to task undoing years of capitalist influence on the southern half of the country.
sentences.zh: 越南社会主义共和国新政府立即着手消除多年来资本主义对该国南部地区的影响。

sentences.en: And so they embarked on a number of measures, you know, that affected all of Vietnam, but especially South Vietnamese, right?
sentences.zh: 于是他们采取了一系列措施，你知道，这些措施影响了整个越南，但尤其是南越，对吧？

sentences.en: This vision of establishing a socialist paradise, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 也就是所谓的建立社会主义天堂的愿景。

sentences.en: This included changing the currency of Vietnam to undercut the wealthy elites and forcibly relocating roughly a million southerners.
sentences.zh: 这包括更换越南货币以削弱富裕精英阶层，并强行迁移了大约一百万南方人。

sentences.en: But the most infamous post-war policy was incarcerating former South Vietnamese military officers, religious leaders, journalists, academics, artists,
sentences.zh: 但战后最臭名昭著的政策是监禁前南越军官、宗教领袖、记者、学者、艺术家，

sentences.en: basically anyone who didn't agree with the North Vietnamese government in re-education camps, where they spent years starving and forced into manual labor.
sentences.zh: 基本上任何不同意北越政府的人，都被送进再教育营，在那里他们忍饥挨饿，被迫从事体力劳动多年。

sentences.en: After the country reunified, South Vietnam didn't just lose its political recognition and its spot on the map.
sentences.zh: 国家统一后，南越不仅失去了政治承认和在地图上的位置。

sentences.en: It was actively erased.
sentences.zh: 它被彻底抹去了。

sentences.en: The government confiscated records, cassette tapes, right, of music produced, you know, in South Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 政府没收了记录，还有磁带，你知道，就是南越制作的音乐。

sentences.en: They confiscated, you know, hundreds of thousands of books and magazines that were published in, you know, in South Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 他们没收了，你知道，成千上万在南越出版的书籍和杂志。

sentences.en: You know, and many of them were burned.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其中许多都被烧毁了。

sentences.en: So when the first wave of South Vietnamese refugees settled in other parts of the world in the late 70s and early 80s, that music, history,
sentences.zh: 所以当第一批南越难民在70年代末和80年代初定居世界各地时，那些音乐、历史，

sentences.en: and culture became the responsibility of the diaspora.
sentences.zh: 以及文化就成了海外侨民的责任。

sentences.en: Which is why the flag is so important to people like my mom.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这面旗帜对我妈妈这样的人来说如此重要。

sentences.en: We cherish that flag since the day that we fled the country and we don't have the land anymore.
sentences.zh: 从我们逃离国家的那天起，我们就珍视那面旗帜，因为我们已经失去了那片土地。

sentences.en: We just, you know, have the flag.
sentences.zh: 我们只是，你知道，拥有这面旗帜。

sentences.en: Thuan Wong says that for a lot of early Vietnamese American refugees, the yellow flag with red stripes stands for more than an allegiance to a non-existent country.
sentences.zh: Thuan Wong 说，对于许多早期的越南裔美国难民来说，这面黄底红条旗代表的不仅仅是对一个不存在国家的忠诚。

sentences.en: It also represents a different, less commonly told perspective on the Vietnam War.
sentences.zh: 它还代表了关于越南战争的一种不同的、鲜为人知的视角。

sentences.en: There are enough history books and documentaries on the subject to keep any retired dead occupied for years.
sentences.zh: 关于这个主题的历史书籍和纪录片多到足以让任何退休的人看上几年。

sentences.en: But these are all about America's role in the war, America's mistakes, America's loss.
sentences.zh: 但这些书和片子讲的都是美国在战争中的角色、美国的错误、美国的失败。

sentences.en: Even the most visible monument to the war, the Vietnam Veterans Memorial in D.C., was a tribute to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 即使是战争中最显眼的纪念碑，位于华盛顿特区的越南退伍军人纪念碑，也是为了向美国

sentences.en: service members.
sentences.zh: 服役人员致敬。

sentences.en: But really, really, really, there was hardly anything that represents the South Vietnamese experience.
sentences.zh: 但真的，真的，真的，几乎没有任何东西能代表南越人的经历。

sentences.en: The South Vietnamese flag did that.
sentences.zh: 南越国旗做到了这一点。

sentences.en: For the generation that fled the country, it became a banner, a memorial, and a link connecting the South Vietnamese scattered all around the world.
sentences.zh: 对于逃离该国的那一代人来说，它成了一面旗帜、一座纪念碑，以及连接散布在世界各地的南越人的纽带。

sentences.en: As the U.S.
sentences.zh: 随着美国

sentences.en: rekindled diplomatic relations with Vietnam in the late 80s and 90s, a new wave of migration took place to the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 在80年代末和90年代与越南恢复外交关系，新一波移民潮涌向西方。

sentences.en: Many of those South Vietnamese had been political prisoners after the fall of Saigon.
sentences.zh: 许多南越人在西贡陷落后曾是政治犯。

sentences.en: So to them, seeing this flag flying abroad took on new meaning that wasn't just about nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 因此对他们来说，在国外看到这面旗帜飘扬有了新的意义，而不仅仅是怀旧。

sentences.en: The experience of Vietnamese, right, who were living difficult lives in Vietnam after the war, right, and who eventually came to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那些在战后越南过着艰难生活的越南人的经历，对吧，他们最终来到了美国，

sentences.en: I mean, you know, Canada and so on, right.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道，加拿大等等，对吧。

sentences.en: They experienced it as a symbol of freedom, you know, post-war freedom.
sentences.zh: 他们将其视为自由的象征，你知道，战后的自由。

sentences.en: Municipalities all over the world actually fly the South Vietnamese flag out of respect for local Vietnamese communities.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的市政当局实际上都会悬挂南越国旗，以示对当地越南社区的尊重。

sentences.en: And it has been reclassified as the freedom and heritage flag in a number of cities across the country.
sentences.zh: 它在全国许多城市被重新定义为自由与遗产旗帜。

sentences.en: If you spend enough time in a Vietnamese enclave, you might end up thinking that this was the official flag of Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 如果你在越南人聚居区待得足够久，你可能会以为这就是越南的官方国旗。

sentences.en: I 100% grew up thinking that.
sentences.zh: 我百分之百是这样长大的。

sentences.en: I actually remember the day that I found out Vietnam's official flag was something different.
sentences.zh: 我确实记得我发现越南官方国旗是另一回事的那一天。

sentences.en: I was in sixth grade, and our social studies class was assigned a project.
sentences.zh: 当时我上六年级，社会研究课布置了一个项目。

sentences.en: It was something that you've probably had to do at some point in grade school.
sentences.zh: 这可能是你在小学时都做过的事情。

sentences.en: It was a country report.
sentences.zh: 那是一份国家报告。

sentences.en: You choose a nation and then compile a bunch of data, tuck it into a neat little binder, and then present it to the rest of your class.
sentences.zh: 你选择一个国家，然后收集一堆数据，把它装进一个整洁的小活页夹里，然后向全班展示。

sentences.en: Being Vietnamese-American and also wanting to put in as little effort as possible, I naturally chose Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 作为越南裔美国人，又想尽可能少花力气，我自然选择了越南。

sentences.en: But part of the assignment was to draw a picture of that nation's flag, so I booted up in Carta 95, a program that I was using well into the year 2001,
sentences.zh: 但作业的一部分是画出那个国家的国旗，所以我启动了《Encarta 95》，一个我一直用到2001年的程序，

sentences.en: and used some colored pencils to transpose the graphic that I saw onto a sheet of paper.
sentences.zh: 并用彩色铅笔把我在上面看到的图案画在了一张纸上。

sentences.en: It was a red field with a bright yellow five-pointed star at the center.
sentences.zh: 那是一面红色的旗帜，中间有一颗明亮的黄色五角星。

sentences.en: I didn't recognize this flag, but who was I to question in Carta 95?
sentences.zh: 我不认识这面旗帜，但我有什么资格质疑《Encarta 95》呢？

sentences.en: The morning my project was due, my dad was horrified at the sight of that five-pointed star on my homework.
sentences.zh: 项目截止的那天早上，我爸爸看到我作业上的那颗五角星时感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: And that reaction is pretty common amongst South Vietnamese refugees.
sentences.zh: 这种反应在南越难民中相当普遍。

sentences.en: You would not want to show that flag.
sentences.zh: 你肯定不想展示那面旗帜。

sentences.en: Yeah, people wouldn't really throw things at you.
sentences.zh: 是啊，人们不会真的拿东西扔你。

sentences.en: A lot of refugees see the official flag, the red flag with the yellow five-pointed star, as a reminder of what they'd fled in Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 许多难民将官方国旗，即带有黄色五角星的红旗，视为他们从越南逃离的痛苦回忆。

sentences.en: So as Vietnamese-Americans became more politically active in the 90s and early 2000s, essentially anywhere the official flag appeared, a protest would follow.
sentences.zh: 随着越南裔美国人在90年代和21世纪初变得更加活跃，基本上只要官方旗帜出现的地方，抗议活动就会随之而来。

sentences.en: They were a constant thing.
sentences.zh: 它们是常态。

sentences.en: Every weekend, you know, in Little Saigon, there was a protest that was somewhat related to the flag.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每个周末在小西贡，都会有与那面旗帜相关的抗议活动。

sentences.en: The biggest incident happened in 1999 at a suburban strip mall right at the heart of Orange County's Little Saigon.
sentences.zh: 最大的冲突发生在1999年，地点就在奥兰治县小西贡中心的一个郊区购物中心。

sentences.en: Actually, just two blocks from where my parents worked.
sentences.zh: 实际上，离我父母工作的地方只有两个街区。

sentences.en: The scene was reminiscent of the 60s, row after row of police in full riot gear.
sentences.zh: 那场景让人回想起60年代，一排排全副武装的防暴警察。

sentences.en: Civil disobedience leads...
sentences.zh: 公民抗命导致……

sentences.en: The owner of a video store called High Tech TV and VCR was a recent immigrant from Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 一家名为“高科技电视与录像机”的音像店老板是一位刚从越南移民过来的人。

sentences.en: And he decided to put up the red flag along with a portrait of Ho Chi Minh.
sentences.zh: 他决定挂出那面红旗，旁边还挂着胡志明的肖像。

sentences.en: The owner in this case was kind of asking for trouble.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，店主简直是在自找麻烦。

sentences.en: Well, he was literally asking for trouble.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他确实是在自找麻烦。

sentences.en: The store owner actually sent fax messages to local Vietnamese community leaders, detailing what he had done and daring them to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 店主甚至给当地越南社区领袖发了传真，详细说明了自己的所作所为，并挑衅他们对此采取行动。

sentences.en: The protest lasted for months.
sentences.zh: 抗议活动持续了数月。

sentences.en: And at its peak, the LA Times recorded over 15,000 protesters in one day.
sentences.zh: 在高峰期，《洛杉矶时报》记录到一天内有超过15000名抗议者。

sentences.en: I used to get my hair cut in this plaza, and I cannot imagine that many people cramming into that little parking lot.
sentences.zh: 我以前常在这个广场理发，我无法想象那么多人挤进那个小停车场的情景。

sentences.en: Thuy Vo Deng actually went to these protests back in 1999 and could see that, yes, the official red star flag was capable of setting off a firestorm of controversy.
sentences.zh: Thuy Vo Deng在1999年确实参加过这些抗议活动，她亲眼看到，是的，那面官方的红星旗确实能引发一场巨大的争议风暴。

sentences.en: But the yellow flag of South Vietnam could also be a polarizing symbol, especially when you think about who is excluded and what kind of conversations are shut down by it.
sentences.zh: 但南越的黄旗也可能是一个两极分化的象征，尤其是当你考虑到谁被排斥在外，以及它会阻断什么样的对话时。

sentences.en: It is the only flag allowed in Little Saigon.
sentences.zh: 它是小西贡唯一被允许悬挂的旗帜。

sentences.en: So that is a certain kind of sanctioning as well, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这也是一种认可，对吧？

sentences.en: And how do people who have immigrated here very recently have grown up in Vietnam with the red flag only?
sentences.zh: 那么，那些最近才移民到这里，在越南只见过红旗长大的人们又该如何自处呢？

sentences.en: How do they feel around the Lunar New Year when they walk around Bolsa Avenue and only see the yellow flag?
sentences.zh: 当他们在农历新年期间走在博尔萨大道上，却只看到黄旗时，他们会有什么感觉？

sentences.en: The South Vietnamese flag could be especially inciting when used in community politics.
sentences.zh: 南越旗帜在社区政治中使用时，尤其具有煽动性。

sentences.en: If the official five-pointed star flag of Vietnam is viewed as the communist flag, then the yellow flag with red stripes of South Vietnam is seen as the anti-communist flag.
sentences.zh: 如果说越南官方的五角星旗被视为共产主义旗帜，那么南越的黄底红条旗就被视为反共旗帜。

sentences.en: When you call someone a communist in the Little Saigon community, that's like a death knell for their political career, right?
sentences.zh: 在小西贡社区，当你称呼某人为共产主义者时，这就像是他们政治生涯的丧钟，对吧？

sentences.en: It's slanderous.
sentences.zh: 这是诽谤。

sentences.en: It's like, so, I mean, I've seen it used in ways that have been intended to cause harm, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我见过它被用来造成伤害，对吧？

sentences.en: To leverage the emotional weight that we've put to this flag, right?
sentences.zh: 利用我们赋予这面旗帜的情感重量，对吧？

sentences.en: And try to hurt others.
sentences.zh: 并试图伤害他人。

sentences.en: These staunch anti-communist views are actually a big part of why first-generation Vietnamese Americans have always been a pretty reliable Republican voting bloc.
sentences.zh: 这些坚定的反共观点，实际上是第一代越南裔美国人一直以来都是相当可靠的共和党选民的重要原因。

sentences.en: That, and a lot of Vietnamese people, also tend to be drawn to the GOP's hardline stance on China, which I don't agree with.
sentences.zh: 这一点，再加上许多越南人也倾向于被共和党对华强硬的立场所吸引，虽然我并不认同这一点。

sentences.en: But apparently a thousand years of occupation and territorial disputes can lead to a pretty gnarly grudge.
sentences.zh: 但显然，千年的占领和领土争端会导致相当深刻的积怨。

sentences.en: That is something that we can actually generalize meaningfully.
sentences.zh: 这是我们可以有意义地概括的一点。

sentences.en: The easiest way to anger a Vietnamese is just say something nice about China.
sentences.zh: 让越南人生气的最简单方法，就是说中国的好话。

sentences.en: The South Vietnamese flag has been drifting towards politically conservative symbolism for a while now.
sentences.zh: 南越旗帜在一段时间以来，已经逐渐演变成政治保守主义的象征。

sentences.en: For some, the yellow flag with red stripes has become a shorthand for right-wing nationalism.
sentences.zh: 对一些人来说，黄底红条旗已经成了右翼民族主义的代名词。

sentences.en: It had been a constant presence at Trump rallies leading up to January 6th.
sentences.zh: 在1月6日事件之前，它在特朗普的集会上一直频繁出现。

sentences.en: So many of us in the community weren't even surprised to see it at the insurrection.
sentences.zh: 所以我们社区里的许多人看到它出现在暴乱现场时，甚至一点也不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: You can see at least half a dozen protesters scaling, literally...
sentences.zh: 你可以看到至少有六名抗议者正在攀爬，真的……

sentences.en: I was disheartened.
sentences.zh: 我感到很沮丧。

sentences.en: I was, you know, I was angry.
sentences.zh: 我，你知道，我很生气。

sentences.en: I was frustrated, all of those things, but I wasn't surprised.
sentences.zh: 我感到挫败，所有这些情绪都有，但我并不惊讶。

sentences.en: There's a huge generational divide in the Vietnamese community when it comes to politics.
sentences.zh: 在越南社区，谈到政治时存在巨大的代沟。

sentences.en: So much so that there's even a support group on Facebook for Asian-Americans with Republican parents that's filled with second-generation Vietnamese kids.
sentences.zh: 以至于Facebook上甚至有一个专门为有共和党父母的亚裔美国人建立的支持小组，里面全是第二代越南裔孩子。

sentences.en: Like a lot of conservative America, Republican Vietnamese have been drawn to Trumpism.
sentences.zh: 像许多保守派美国人一样，共和党越南裔也被特朗普主义所吸引。

sentences.en: And for the older generation especially, the ones who experienced the war, there could still be a deep fear of communism.
sentences.zh: 尤其是对于老一辈人，那些经历过战争的人来说，内心深处可能仍然对共产主义有着深深的恐惧。

sentences.en: So when they hear stuff like this...
sentences.zh: 所以当他们听到这样的言论时……

sentences.en: Like it or not, we are becoming a communist country.
sentences.zh: 不管你喜不喜欢，我们正在变成一个共产主义国家。

sentences.en: That's what's happening.
sentences.zh: 这就是正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: That pulls on actual, lived trauma.
sentences.zh: 这触动了他们真实经历过的创伤。

sentences.en: The people who brought the South Vietnamese flag to the insurrection only represented a very small and very noisy subsect of the community.
sentences.zh: 那些把南越旗帜带到暴乱现场的人，只代表了社区中极小且非常吵闹的一小部分。

sentences.en: Most people, including my mom, hated seeing the flag there that day.
sentences.zh: 大多数人，包括我妈妈，那天看到那面旗帜出现在那里都感到很反感。

sentences.en: That day, that January 6th, right?
sentences.zh: 那天，就是1月6日那天，对吧？

sentences.en: There's a lot of, you know, debate after that in the community.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，社区里确实有很多，你知道的，争论。

sentences.en: There's a lot of people againSt.
sentences.zh: 很多人反对。

sentences.en: That people bring the flag to that event, you know?
sentences.zh: 反对人们把那面旗帜带到那场活动中，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And me too, I don't like it.
sentences.zh: 我也是，我不喜欢它。

sentences.en: In the days following January 6th, a number of write-ups were published to help people, quote,
sentences.zh: 在1月6日之后的几天里，发表了许多文章来帮助人们，引用一下，

sentences.en: decode some of the racist imagery of the insurrection.
sentences.zh: 解读暴乱中出现的一些种族主义意象。

sentences.en: And some of them included the South Vietnamese flag.
sentences.zh: 其中一些文章提到了南越旗帜。

sentences.en: I felt queasy seeing it lumped in with all these symbols of hate.
sentences.zh: 看到它与所有这些仇恨符号混在一起，我感到很不舒服。

sentences.en: For a large swath of the U.S., January 6th was probably the first time they'd even seen the South Vietnamese flag.
sentences.zh: 对于美国很大一部分人来说，1月6日可能是他们第一次见到南越旗帜。

sentences.en: It is not far-fetched to think that some observers may have wondered what radical group this yellow flag with red stripes represented.
sentences.zh: 认为一些观察者可能想知道这面带有红条纹的黄旗代表什么激进组织，这并不牵强。

sentences.en: The South Vietnamese flag's presence that day brought up a lot of questions for those of us who don't want to see it end up like Pepe the Frog.
sentences.zh: 南越旗帜那天出现在现场，对于我们这些不想看到它最终变成像“佩佩蛙”那样符号的人来说，引发了很多疑问。

sentences.en: But Thuy Vo Deng thinks that this doesn't just have to be an embarrassing moment for the Vietnamese-American community.
sentences.zh: 但Thuy Vo Deng认为，这不一定非得是越南裔美国人社区的一个尴尬时刻。

sentences.en: It could also be an opportunity to face our history before it gets co-opted by any side of the political spectrum.
sentences.zh: 这也可以是一个机会，让我们在它被政治光谱的任何一方挪用之前，直面我们的历史。

sentences.en: It's up to us to do the work of pushing the conversation towards understanding the nuances and complexities of our history.
sentences.zh: 我们有责任去努力推动对话，去理解我们历史中的细微差别和复杂性。

sentences.en: But I think, you know, all of the attention that came after the appearance of the yellow flag at the insurrection could enable an entry point.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，你知道，暴乱中出现黄旗后引起的所有关注，可能提供了一个切入点。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people in my generation have a very different relationship to this flag and to Vietnam itself.
sentences.zh: 我认为我这一代人中的许多人，与这面旗帜以及越南本身有着非常不同的关系。

sentences.en: To me, the flag just can't be boiled down to freedom or nostalgia or anti-communism or any of the other one-liners ascribed to it.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这面旗帜不能简单地归结为自由、怀旧、反共，或者任何其他被贴在它身上的标签。

sentences.en: It's a complex symbol for the complicated history of how I got here.
sentences.zh: 它是一个复杂的符号，代表了我如何来到这里的复杂历史。

sentences.en: When I just started up my life here, I missed everything, you know, in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 当我刚开始在这里生活时，我怀念过去的一切，你知道的。

sentences.en: But now it's okay.
sentences.zh: 但现在没关系了。

sentences.en: I like it here.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这里。

sentences.en: I hadn't really thought about it before.
sentences.zh: 我以前真的没想过这个问题。

sentences.en: But my mom's life directly reflects the yellow flag with red stripes.
sentences.zh: 但我妈妈的生活直接反映了那面带红条纹的黄旗。

sentences.en: She was born in 1955, the same year that South Vietnam was created.
sentences.zh: 她出生于1955年，也就是南越成立的那一年。

sentences.en: And she fled the country in 1975, the year it ended.
sentences.zh: 她在1975年逃离了这个国家，那也是它终结的一年。

sentences.en: I just spent 20 years on my life, first life in Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 我刚在越南度过了我生命的前20年。

sentences.en: And now I'm 66, so more than the book here in the United States.
sentences.zh: 现在我66岁了，在美国生活的时间比在越南长了。

sentences.en: So I love this country.
sentences.zh: 所以我爱这个国家。

sentences.en: My mom said something that stuck with me that I think applies to the flag of South Vietnam too.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈说的一句话让我印象深刻，我认为这也适用于南越旗帜。

sentences.en: She doesn't want to live in the past, but she doesn't want to forget it either.
sentences.zh: 她不想活在过去，但她也不想忘记过去。

sentences.en: She wants the same for me too.
sentences.zh: 她也希望我能这样。

sentences.en: Because one day, the war will stop being a living memory and just be history.
sentences.zh: 因为总有一天，战争将不再是鲜活的记忆，而仅仅成为历史。

sentences.en: And what we'll be left with is a yellow flag with red stripes.
sentences.zh: 而留给我们的，将是一面带红条纹的黄旗。

sentences.en: After the break, Vivian comes back to help decode the hidden history behind Vietnamese restaurant names.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，Vivian将回来帮助解读越南餐馆名称背后的隐藏历史。

sentences.en: So we're back with Vivian Le.
sentences.zh: 我们又回到了Vivian Le的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for that story.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你带来的那个故事。

sentences.en: I always love the stories where I learn a little bit more about you guys' lives.
sentences.zh: 我总是喜欢那些能让我更多了解你们生活的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah, and talk to our parents too.
sentences.zh: 是的，也要和我们的父母聊聊。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because I'm going to talk about pho restaurants.
sentences.zh: 因为我要谈谈河粉店。

sentences.en: So if any listeners don't know what pho is, I feel bad for you because it's so good.
sentences.zh: 如果还有听众不知道什么是河粉，我真为你感到遗憾，因为它太好吃了。

sentences.en: It's probably the most visible dish that has come out of Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 它可能是越南最广为人知的菜肴。

sentences.en: Like when I meet someone and they find out I'm Vietnamese and they don't know how to make conversation a lot of times,
sentences.zh: 就像当我遇到某人，他们发现我是越南人，而他们不知道该聊什么的时候，很多时候，

sentences.en: they'll be like, well, I like pho.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，嗯，我喜欢河粉。

sentences.en: I'm like, okay, great.
sentences.zh: 我就说，好的，太棒了。

sentences.en: Thank you for that.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你的分享。

sentences.en: But I guess to boil it down to its most basic level, it's like a noodle plus protein plus fragrant broth soup.
sentences.zh: 但我想把它归结为最基本的层面，它就是一种面条加蛋白质加上香浓肉汤的汤品。

sentences.en: And it has like bean sprouts and Thai basil and lime and onions.
sentences.zh: 里面还有豆芽、泰国罗勒、青柠和洋葱。

sentences.en: You're given a kit when you get it.
sentences.zh: 你吃的时候会配上一套佐料。

sentences.en: It's like it is really the greatest soup.
sentences.zh: 它简直就是最棒的汤。

sentences.en: And I know that that's a contentious subject when it comes to a lot of people and a lot of soups in different cultures.
sentences.zh: 我知道在很多人和不同文化背景的汤品中，这是一个有争议的话题。

sentences.en: But I'm here to tell you, pho is the beSt.
sentences.zh: 但我还是要告诉你，越南河粉（pho）就是最棒的。

sentences.en: Oh, it's the best soup.
sentences.zh: 哦，它是最棒的汤。

sentences.en: Yeah, the accoutrements alone that come with the bowl of pho.
sentences.zh: 没错，光是那碗河粉里配的佐料就够讲究了。

sentences.en: But, you know, if you if you drive through pretty much any little Saigon in the world,
sentences.zh: 不过，你知道，如果你开车穿过世界上任何一个“小西贡”，

sentences.en: you would probably notice that there's this really common naming convention when it comes to pho restaurants.
sentences.zh: 你可能会注意到越南河粉店有一个非常普遍的命名惯例。

sentences.en: And I think it's really well articulated by Ali Wong in her comedy special Baby Cobra.
sentences.zh: 我觉得黄阿丽（Ali Wong）在她的喜剧专场《小眼镜蛇》（Baby Cobra）中对此阐述得非常到位。

sentences.en: So Wong herself is Vietnamese.
sentences.zh: 黄阿丽本人就是越南裔。

sentences.en: And there's this part where she's talking about how her now husband tried to take her to like a quote authentic Vietnamese restaurant on one of their first dates.
sentences.zh: 她讲到她现在的丈夫在他们第一次约会时，试图带她去一家所谓的“正宗”越南餐厅。

sentences.en: He took me to this restaurant on the west side of Los Angeles called pho show.
sentences.zh: 他带我去了洛杉矶西区一家叫“Pho Show”的餐厅。

sentences.en: He was like, it's authentic Vietnamese.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是正宗的越南菜。

sentences.en: I read about it on Yelp.
sentences.zh: 我在Yelp上看到的。

sentences.en: I was like, it's not authentic.
sentences.zh: 我说，这不正宗。

sentences.en: OK, you can tell first and foremost by the name because it don't got a number in it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你首先可以通过名字看出来，因为它名字里没有数字。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So she's talking about this completely valid stereotype about Vietnamese restaurants that they're always named like the word pho plus a seemingly random number.
sentences.zh: 所以她谈论的是关于越南餐厅一个完全成立的刻板印象，那就是它们的名字总是“Pho”加上一个看似随机的数字。

sentences.en: Like right now I'm looking at a map of Orange County and there's a pho 99 right next to a pho 86, which is less than a block away from a pho 45.
sentences.zh: 比如我现在看奥兰治县的地图，有一家“Pho 99”紧挨着“Pho 86”，离“Pho 45”不到一个街区。

sentences.en: And then there's a pho 54 around the corner from a pho 79, which is very good, by the way.
sentences.zh: 然后拐角处还有一家“Pho 54”和“Pho 79”，顺便说一下，那家店很好吃。

sentences.en: It's a great restaurant.
sentences.zh: 那是一家很棒的餐厅。

sentences.en: So there's this very, very common thing that you will see with Vietnamese restaurants that they always kind of include a number.
sentences.zh: 所以，你在越南餐厅里会看到这种非常、非常普遍的现象，它们总是会带上一个数字。

sentences.en: So what's the number all about?
sentences.zh: 那么这些数字到底是什么意思呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So sometimes the restaurant will have a number just because like the numbers themselves are lucky.
sentences.zh: 有时候餐厅用数字仅仅是因为数字本身很吉利。

sentences.en: Like if you see a pho 555 or a pho 888, it's because five and eight are like auspicious numbers in a lot of Eastern cultures.
sentences.zh: 比如如果你看到“Pho 555”或“Pho 888”，那是因为在许多东方文化中，五和八是吉祥数字。

sentences.en: Plus, it's like super memorable to have like three numbers in a row.
sentences.zh: 而且，连续三个相同的数字非常容易让人记住。

sentences.en: But if you pay close enough attention to the numbers, they can actually tell you about the restaurant's owner's family history or the history of Vietnam in general.
sentences.zh: 但如果你足够留意这些数字，它们实际上可以告诉你餐厅老板的家族史，或者越南的历史。

sentences.en: So if you see a restaurant called like pho 86 or pho 79, that could represent that the owner of the restaurant immigrated from Vietnam in 1986 or in 1979.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你看到一家叫“Pho 86”或“Pho 79”的餐厅，那可能代表店主是在1986年或1979年从越南移民出来的。

sentences.en: So that's a really common naming convention in Vietnamese American culture.
sentences.zh: 这是美籍越南文化中一种非常普遍的命名惯例。

sentences.en: And it's this way to kind of pay tribute to the start of this new life.
sentences.zh: 这是一种向新生活起点致敬的方式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like around our office in Oakland, we have a pho 84, which I like to visit.
sentences.zh: 比如在我们奥克兰的办公室附近，有一家“Pho 84”，我喜欢去那儿吃。

sentences.en: So my guess is 84 makes it one of those ones where it's indicative of a year.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜84也属于那种代表年份的数字。

sentences.en: Like, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错，没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: Like usually the numbers are signifying some sort of year.
sentences.zh: 通常这些数字都代表着某种年份。

sentences.en: So you'll also see a lot of places named like pho 75 specifically.
sentences.zh: 你还会看到很多叫“Pho 75”的店。

sentences.en: And 75 is a really important number in Vietnamese American culture because 1975 is the year of the fall of Saigon and the end of South Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 75在美籍越南文化中是一个非常重要的数字，因为1975年是西贡陷落和南越灭亡的年份。

sentences.en: So a lot of Vietnamese Americans actually commemorate it every year with something called Black April,
sentences.zh: 所以很多美籍越南人每年都会纪念它，称之为“黑色四月”（Black April），

sentences.en: which marks the day that Saigon fell on April 30th, 1975.
sentences.zh: 标志着西贡在1975年4月30日陷落的那一天。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I've never heard of Black April.
sentences.zh: 我从没听说过“黑色四月”。

sentences.en: That's really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太令人着迷了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's celebrated mostly in like little Saigons and stuff.
sentences.zh: 它主要是在“小西贡”之类的地方庆祝。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it was a big thing where I was growing up.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，在我成长的地方，这可是件大事。

sentences.en: So you might see a lot of pho 75s because there was a lot of immigration activity in 1975 because of the fall of Saigon.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会看到很多“Pho 75”，因为西贡陷落导致1975年有大量的移民活动。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So another restaurant number you'll probably see a lot is pho 54.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会经常看到的另一个餐厅数字是“Pho 54”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we talk about this.
sentences.zh: 我们来聊聊这个。

sentences.en: We talk about 54 in the piece.
sentences.zh: 我们在文章里提到了54年。

sentences.en: So this is when the creation of South Vietnam, the partitioning of the country.
sentences.zh: 那是南越建立、国家分裂的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: So this is when Vietnam was split basically into North and South Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 所以当时越南基本上被分成了北越和南越。

sentences.en: And this is actually a really big date in Vietnamese food culture as well, because, you know, when the country was split in two,
sentences.zh: 这对越南饮食文化来说也是一个非常重要的时间点，因为你知道，当国家一分为二时，

sentences.en: there was this huge migration of people between North and South Vietnam because the North was now communist country.
sentences.zh: 北越和南越之间发生了大规模的人口迁移，因为北越现在是共产主义国家了。

sentences.en: The South was now anti-communiSt. So in the U.S., they called this Operation Passage to Freedom.
sentences.zh: 而南越是反共的。在美国，这被称为“自由之路行动”。

sentences.en: But essentially, it was this grace period where people were allowed to flee the North or the South before the border was officially sealed.
sentences.zh: 但本质上，这是一个宽限期，在边境正式封锁之前，人们被允许从北越逃往南越。

sentences.en: So somewhere between 600,000 to a million North Vietnamese actually relocated to the South.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上有60万到100万北越人迁往了南方。

sentences.en: And this is actually how my mom's family ended up in Saigon because they were part of this migration from the North to the South.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈的家人就是这样来到西贡的，因为他们也是这次从北向南大迁徙的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But this was important for like Vietnamese food culture specifically, too, because pho is a dish that actually originated from North Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 但这对于越南饮食文化也特别重要，因为河粉（pho）这道菜其实起源于北越。

sentences.en: So for a long time, pho wasn't actually something that was eaten very much in South Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 所以很长一段时间里，河粉在南越其实并不怎么流行。

sentences.en: Like if you've ever been there, it's very, very hot and you steam you there.
sentences.zh: 如果你去过那里，就会知道那里非常非常热，而且很潮湿。

sentences.en: But it became really popular in the South because this huge influx of Northerners that relocated to places like Saigon.
sentences.zh: 但随着大量北方人迁往西贡等地，它在南方变得非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: And pho itself changed a lot after it was brought to South Vietnam because of the available ingredients like in South Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 而且河粉本身在被带到南越后发生了很大变化，因为南越有各种各样的食材。

sentences.en: So originally it was pretty simple, but that's when we started putting like the herbs and the bean sprouts and just packing it with all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 最初它很简单，但后来我们开始加入香草、豆芽，塞进各种配料。

sentences.en: And so this kind of hybrid North-South version of pho is what was taken abroad when Vietnamese started immigrating to other parts of the world after the war.
sentences.zh: 这种南北融合版的河粉，就是后来战争结束后越南人移民到世界各地时带出去的版本。

sentences.en: Oh, that's cool.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太酷了。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: And so actually this tradition of naming restaurants to include a number in it, like an important date or something,
sentences.zh: 其实，用数字（比如重要的日期之类）来命名餐馆的传统，

sentences.en: is actually something that you mostly see in the older restaurants, like by people who are the first generation immigrants.
sentences.zh: 主要出现在老字号餐馆里，也就是第一代移民开的那些店。

sentences.en: So newer Vietnamese restaurants tend to be, you know, less likely to adhere to that like numbered name convention.
sentences.zh: 所以较新的越南餐馆往往不太会遵循这种数字命名的惯例。

sentences.en: So the stereotype about it not being like, quote, authentic, like a quote, authentic Vietnamese restaurant kind of comes from somewhere just because, you know,
sentences.zh: 关于“不正宗”的刻板印象，也就是所谓的“不正宗”越南餐馆，其实是有据可循的，因为，你知道，

sentences.en: the places with the numbers will be more old school, more traditional.
sentences.zh: 那些名字里带数字的店往往更老派、更传统。

sentences.en: Like I personally try to avoid anything with like a pun on the word pho in it, you know, like a restaurant called pho-nominal or something.
sentences.zh: 比如我个人尽量避开那些在“pho”这个词上玩谐音梗的店，你知道，比如叫“pho-nominal”之类的餐馆。

sentences.en: I'm like, no, not for me.
sentences.zh: 我会觉得，不，那不是我的菜。

sentences.en: Well, especially ones that, you know, imply that pho rhymes with show or that it's pho.
sentences.zh: 尤其是那些暗示“pho”和“show”押韵，或者读作“foe”的店。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，确实。

sentences.en: That is my biggest pet peeve.
sentences.zh: 那是我最受不了的事。

sentences.en: It's pho.
sentences.zh: 是“fuh”。

sentences.en: It's not pho.
sentences.zh: 不是“foe”。

sentences.en: Please, please, please, please know.
sentences.zh: 求求你们，一定要记住了。

sentences.en: Take anything from this coda.
sentences.zh: 如果这期节目你只记得住一件事，

sentences.en: Pho.
sentences.zh: 那就是“fuh”。

sentences.en: Say, do pho.
sentences.zh: 试着读一下，fuh。

sentences.en: Do your best you can.
sentences.zh: 尽你所能去读。

sentences.en: Just remember pho.
sentences.zh: 只要记住是“fuh”就行。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, this is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太令人着迷了。

sentences.en: I love the idea that you could, you know, drive through a neighborhood and just know a family's history from the names of the pho places.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这种想法：你可以开车穿过一个街区，仅凭河粉店的名字就能了解一个家庭的历史。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the cooleSt.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这太酷了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, thank you, Vivian.
sentences.zh: 那么，谢谢你，Vivian。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你。
